description: The National Plan of Integrated Airport Systems (NPIAS) is the Federal Aviation Administration's list of airports significant to US civil aviation and eligible for federal funding under the Airport Improvement Program and the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, with estimates of their development needs. The 2025-2029 edition, published on 30 September 2024 with the narrative updated in July 2026, includes 3,287 existing public-use airports and five proposed nonprimary airports expected to open by 2029, assigns each airport a category (390 primary airports on 2023 data), and estimates about 67.5 billion dollars of eligible and justified development for 2025 to 2029, up about 5.1 billion from the previous edition; primary airports account for 72 percent of that cost. Appendix A lists every airport with its category and development estimate in XLSX and PDF, Appendix B gives national and state maps, and further appendices define terms and compliance land use. Access: free downloads from the FAA page. Licence and cost: US Government work, free. Caveats: costs are airport-reported needs for eligible projects, not funded commitments, aggregated by airport, not by project, and the plan is revised every two years. It supports capacity planning and investment scenarios for airport networks. It relates to the FAA air traffic activity and NASR data and OurAirports in the catalogue.
